capabilities: read EPUB, TXT, MOBI/AZW3, FB2, CBZ and PDF files in a bookshelf view
highlight passages and save them as wikilinks that jump back to the source
browse PDFs with page thumbnails, page links, backlinks, and page-to-image export
ask AI questions about the whole book using an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
read books aloud with system, online, or local speech engines
disambiguation: Not just a PDF viewer; it is a full reading shelf for EPUB, TXT, MOBI, AZW3, FB2, comics and PDF.
extras: Freemium: base reading is free; Pro features (most formats, PDF tools, stats, AI, offline audio) need a paid license key verified locally. Several listed 'Explorations' features (OCR, PDF reflow, manga mode, chapter translation, review, E Ink optimization) are marked as not yet available at any tier. Community listing was still pending review at time of writing; BRAT or manual install offered meanwhile.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to read books or PDFs as books, with progress, highlights, and links back into your notes.

relations.evidence: Embeddings come from the bz (second brain) plugin: without it there is no vector search

summary: In-vault ebook reader with a bookshelf that opens EPUB, TXT, MOBI, CBZ and PDF, with highlights as wikilinks, text-to-speech, and AI Q&A.
